s1.syndrome_frame: excessive sweating of the buttocks and sacrum with significant impact on daily life
salient_findings: excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous successful treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis with 20% aluminum chloride
unsuccessful treatment of intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride
key_facts: 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks
most severe sweating at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous treatment with 20% aluminum chloride for axillary hyperhidrosis
unsuccessful treatment of intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride
uses absorbent pads due to severity of the condition
unable to attend work due to the condition
Minor starch-iodine test performed to localize sites of overactive sweating
significant sweating identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)

shortlist.label: Primary Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of axillary hyperhidrosis and now presents with excessive sweating of the buttocks, consistent with primary hyperhidrosis

shortlist.label: Compensatory Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's previous treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis with aluminum chloride may have led to compensatory sweating in other areas, such as the buttocks

shortlist.label: Localized Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's excessive sweating is localized to the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, consistent with localized hyperhidrosis

shortlist.label: Generalized Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although patient's sweating is currently localized, generalized hyperhidrosis is a possible diagnosis given the patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis

shortlist.label: Secondary Hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's excessive sweating may be secondary to an underlying condition, such as autonomic dysfunction or neurogenic disorder, which needs to be ruled out

raw.rationale: The patient's excessive sweating is limited to specific areas, namely the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, which is consistent with localized hyperhidrosis. The Minor starch-iodine test also confirmed significant sweating in these areas.

rejected.label: Primary Hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: Primary hyperhidrosis typically involves multiple areas of the body, such as the palms, soles, and axillae, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Compensatory Hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: Compensatory hyperhidrosis usually occurs in response to another condition, such as hyperthyroidism, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Generalized Hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: Generalized hyperhidrosis involves widespread excessive sweating, which is not consistent with the patient's localized symptoms.

rejected.label: Secondary Hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: Secondary hyperhidrosis is caused by an underlying medical condition, which is not indicated in the vignette.
